notes: Derived edit (very_likely): the largest prime factor of 1729 is never stated in Dolma (0 hits for 'largest prime factor of 1729' and 'greatest prime factor of 1729') and follows from the well-known factorization 1729 = 7 × 13 × 19 and the definition of the largest prime factor. Chosen for coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12): the new relation has_largest_prime_factor has subproperty:has_prime_factor, and has_prime_factor (over composite numbers) has subproperty:multiple_of, so two subproperty queries discriminate (23 a prime factor; 1729 a multiple of 23). Mathematics leaves out worlds (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number or a shape rests on definitions and proofs, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between. Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. The factorization is what gives way, as in replace-0004 (1001). The premise-route query reaches the edited fact through the factorization by description (its last prime in increasing order). 'Is 1729 divisible by 13?' and 'by 7?' were left out: the edit does not say what happens to the smaller factors, so they are not forced. Near: the largest prime factor of 1728 (= 2⁶ × 3³) shares the relation; reference 3 differs from the new answer 23 (Rule 7). The smallest prime factor of 1729 was rejected as near: it comes from the same factorization premise. R2: no prompt names a factor of 1729. The original answer (no) of 'Is 1729 a multiple of 23?' rests on 23 being prime and on a number being a multiple of a prime only if that prime is one of its prime factors (none of 7, 13, 19 is 23); both are bridges with checks.
